edges.description: Without the alpha-1,2-mannosyltransferase step, elongation of Man3GlcNAc2-PP-dolichol cannot proceed and the immature LLO species accumulate.
The oligosaccharyltransferase transfers the available truncated glycan, or fails to transfer at all, so nascent glycoproteins carry incomplete or missing N-glycan chains.
Incomplete N-glycosylation of many unrelated glycoproteins degrades their folding, stability, trafficking and function across organ systems.
Beyond the static encephalopathy, affected brains lose volume over time rather than merely developing abnormally.
Directly measures the accumulating LLO species and the deficient elongation step in cells carrying the patient genotype.
edges.limitations: Fibroblasts are not an affected tissue in this disorder, which is neurological; the assay reports the biochemical lesion faithfully but says nothing about why the brain bears the disease.
edges.source: Patient-derived skin fibroblast lipid-linked oligosaccharide analysis

edges.description: Reports whether a given human ALG11 allele can restore function in a cell lacking the orthologous gene, which is a direct read on the allele's catalytic competence.
edges.limitations: A yeast cell is not a human one: the assay can show that an allele is hypofunctional, but not how much residual activity a human tissue needs, and the ALG11 substrate context differs between the two organisms.
edges.source: Yeast alg11 deletion strain complementation assay

evidence.reference_title: A severe human metabolic disease caused by deficiency of the endoplasmatic mannosyltransferase hALG11 leads to congenital disorder of glycosylation-Ip.
evidence.snippet: Verification of the mutation as a primary cause for the genetic defect was proved by retroviral expression of human wild-type and mutated ALG11 cDNA in patient-derived fibroblasts as well as using a yeast alg11 deletion strain as a heterologous expression system for hALG11 variants.

evidence.reference_title: Improved diagnostics lead to identification of three new patients with congenital disorder of glycosylation-Ip.
evidence.snippet: Although all CDG-Ip patients carry different mutations in the ALG11 gene, they share a variety of clinical syndromes

nodes.description: Biallelic pathogenic ALG11 variants abolish or severely reduce the activity of the ER GDP-mannose:Man3GlcNAc2-PP-dolichol alpha-1,2-mannosyltransferase, the enzyme that sequentially adds the fourth and fifth of the nine mannose residues of the lipid-linked oligosaccharide precursor. The originally described p.Leu86Ser allele does not mislocalize or destabilize the protein, so the lesion is catalytic rather than a loss of the enzyme from the ER.

evidence.reference_title: A severe human metabolic disease caused by deficiency of the endoplasmatic mannosyltransferase hALG11 leads to congenital disorder of glycosylation-Ip.
evidence.snippet: A new type of congenital disorders of glycosylation, designated CDG-Ip, is caused by the deficiency of GDP-Man:Man3GlcNAc2-PP-dolichol-alpha1,2-mannosyltransferase, encoded by the human ortholog of ALG11 from yeast.
encodes the mannosyltransferase that uses GDP-mannose to sequentially add the fourth and the fifth of the nine mannoses to the LLO on the outer leaflet of the endoplasmic reticulum

nodes.description: Seizure control is a central management goal, but epilepsy in ALG11-CDG is frequently drug-resistant. No anti-seizure regimen is established as superior for this disorder, and the treatment is symptomatic rather than disease-modifying.

evidence.snippet: A 31-month-old male patient admitted to our center with complaints of axial hypotonia, drug-resistant myoclonic seizures, microcephaly and deafness.

nodes.description: Widespread glycoprotein dysfunction produces the multisystem phenotype: a severe infantile epileptic encephalopathy with developmental disability, together with growth failure, feeding difficulty, sensorineural hearing loss and ophthalmological involvement. Intellectual disability and epilepsy are the two features present in essentially every reported patient.

evidence.snippet: Intellectual disability and epilepsy are universally present, and all had visual problems, except our patient 1

evidence.reference_title: Improved diagnostics lead to identification of three new patients with congenital disorder of glycosylation-Ip.
evidence.snippet: they share a variety of clinical syndromes like an unremarkable prenatal period followed by developmental delay, psychomotor, and mental retardation, strabismus convergens and seizures occurring in the first year of life

nodes.description: Cultured skin fibroblasts from affected individuals, used to size the dolichol-linked oligosaccharide pool and to assay the mannosyltransferase activities of early LLO biosynthesis. This is the system in which the position of the ALG11 block was established, and in which retroviral expression of wild-type ALG11 rescued the defect.
nodes.id: Patient-derived skin fibroblast lipid-linked oligosaccharide analysis

nodes.description: Serial imaging shows a progressive, regionally ordered neurodegenerative course: severe supratentorial volume loss first, with the cerebellum and brainstem relatively preserved in the neonatal period, followed years later by near-complete loss of the cerebral hemispheres with severe cerebellar atrophy and brainstem volume reduction. Cerebral hypomyelination and corpus callosum hypoplasia accompany the atrophy.

evidence.reference_title: Progressive loss of cerebral structures in ALG11-related congenital disorder of glycosylation.
evidence.snippet: There was near complete loss of cerebral hemispheres, severe cerebellar atrophy, and decreased volume of the brainstem.

evidence.reference_title: ALG11-CDG: novel variant and review of the literature.
evidence.snippet: Progressive cerebral atrophy, hypomyelination and corpus callosum hypoplasia were striking features in brain MRI images taken during our follow-up.

evidence.reference_title: Arrest of Fetal Brain Development in ALG11-Congenital Disorder of Glycosylation.
evidence.snippet: Postnatal brain magnetic resonance imaging found no brain growth during the interval from the fetal to postnatal study.

evidence.reference_title: Arrest of Fetal Brain Development in ALG11-Congenital Disorder of Glycosylation.
evidence.snippet: Arrest of fetal brain development, with image findings consistent with fetal brain disruption sequence, is a previously unreported phenotype of congenital microcephaly in ALG11-congenital disorder of glycosylation.

nodes.description: Serum and cellular glycoproteins carry incomplete N-glycan chains. In serum this appears as the type I transferrin isoform profile of a CDG-I disorder; in fibroblasts the membrane glycoprotein GP130 runs as abnormally truncated isoforms. Because transferrin glycosylation can be normal despite proven disease, cellular readouts are the more reliable demonstration of the defect.

evidence.reference_title: A severe human metabolic disease caused by deficiency of the endoplasmatic mannosyltransferase hALG11 leads to congenital disorder of glycosylation-Ip.
evidence.snippet: The isoelectric focusing pattern of the patient's serum transferrin showed the partial loss of complete N-glycan side chains, which is a characteristic sign for CDG-I.
Surprisingly, one patient presented with normal transferrin glycosylation profile, a feature that has not been reported previously in patients with ALG11-CDG.

nodes.description: A Saccharomyces cerevisiae alg11 deletion strain used as a heterologous expression system for human ALG11 variants. Together with retroviral rescue in patient fibroblasts, it is what established the ALG11 variant as causal rather than merely co-segregating.
nodes.id: Yeast alg11 deletion strain complementation assay
